lessons.title: The Evidence Slide — Speaking & Listening
lessons.objective: Practice listening, discussion and presentation through a traceable classroom case while you use one accurate word.

reading.label: Original instructional text
paragraphs: Ty was at a research presentation. Ty displayed a crowded table on one slide. Ty learned something important.

Here is the clue: the key difference was a three-person change. Ty highlighted the comparison and explained uncertainty. The story ends with this result: the audience identified the main result. We still do not know everything: a clear slide does not guarantee valid evidence.
reading.notice: Core evidence: the key difference was a three-person change
reading.limitation: a clear slide does not guarantee valid evidence

glossary.meaning: The ability to interpret and communicate meaning through images and diagrams.
An observable detail or passage quotation offered to support a claim.
An interpretation based on details, rather than a directly reported event.
Language that limits a claim to what the evidence can support.

mentor.title: Read with a purpose
mentor.body: In this speaking & listening lesson, watch for listening, discussion and presentation. The central learning move is to put two events in order.

mentor.title: Worked example
mentor.body: The reading tells us: “the key difference was a three-person change.” That is a detail. We can point to it when we answer.

mentor.title: Think before answering
mentor.body: Ask: What does the passage actually say? How did Ty respond? What does the text leave undecided?

mentor.title: Sentence frames
mentor.body: I see  •  I think  •  The clue is  •  I can tell

mentor.title: Revision workshop
mentor.body: Recheck your wording against the exact detail “the key difference was a three-person change”. Explain why that detail matters. Avoid treating “a clear slide does not guarantee valid evidence” as a proven universal rule.

mentor.title: Independent practice
mentor.body: Try a new example with the same skill. Read a short text, highlight a precise detail, then write an interpretation that the detail supports. If you have no supporting detail, label the idea as a question.

mentor.title: Apply the pattern
mentor.body: In “The Evidence Slide”, separate these three pieces: observation (the key difference was a three-person change), response (highlighted the comparison and explained uncertainty), and outcome (the audience identified the main result). Explain their relationship without inventing an intervening event.

mentor.title: Self-check
mentor.body: Before submitting: Did you respond directly? Did you include relevant evidence? Did you explain your thinking? Did you preserve the caution that a clear slide does not guarantee valid evidence? Did you reread and revise for clarity?
